content.value_statement: Development teams miss recurring framework and security mistakes during busy reviews. This skill routes code changes to targeted pitfall checks and summarizes review concerns.
actual_capabilities: Identifies code categories from changed file paths and framework keywords.
Maps TanStack Query, Drizzle ORM, Express, React, WebSocket, blockchain, and security topics to focused review skills.
Combines findings from relevant sub-skills into one review report.
Provides a quick checklist for type safety, financial calculations, blockchain transactions, and security controls.
Supports pre-commit review, production debugging, and unfamiliar code review workflows.
limitations: It depends on separate pitfall sub-skills for detailed framework-specific analysis.
It does not run tests, inspect runtime behavior, or prove that code is correct.
It provides checklist-based review guidance, not a replacement for manual security assessment.
It may miss project-specific rules that are not covered by the listed categories.

use_cases.title: Pre-commit quality review
use_cases.description: Check changed frontend, backend, data, and security files before committing work.

use_cases.title: Pull request triage
use_cases.description: Route a pull request to relevant pitfall checks and collect concerns for reviewers.

use_cases.title: Production issue investigation
use_cases.description: Review suspect code areas for known pitfalls after an incident or bug report.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic pitfall review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change set
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these changed files for common development pitfalls. Identify the matching categories and summarize the highest priority concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Check a pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the common pitfalls workflow on this pull request. Group findings by TanStack Query, Drizzle, Express, React, WebSocket, blockchain, and security when relevant.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a production bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this bug-related code for recurring pitfalls. Focus on lifecycle state, database types, API responses, RPC failures, logging, and secrets exposure.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a full-stack audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Map this change set to all relevant pitfall sub-skills, combine their findings, rank risks by impact, and recommend concrete fixes for each affected area.

output_examples.input: A pull request changes React components, API routes, and database schema files.
output_examples.output: The review flags React loading states, Express status code handling, and Drizzle type export checks. It groups each concern by affected area.

output_examples.input: A debugging session includes blockchain RPC failures and WebSocket reconnect issues.
output_examples.output: The report focuses on RPC error handling, gas estimation, transaction simulation, heartbeat checks, and reconnection behavior.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks for security-sensitive pitfall checks before merge.
output_examples.output: The checklist highlights secrets in logs, session key expiry, stored credential encryption, audit logging, and rate limiting.

best_practices: Use the skill after collecting the changed files and the purpose of the change.
Follow up with the relevant specialized pitfall skill when a category matches.
Convert each finding into a concrete code change, test, or reviewer question.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the combined checklist as proof that the code is secure.
Do not run every sub-skill when the change clearly touches only one category.
Do not ignore project-specific conventions when applying generic pitfall guidance.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews common pitfalls across query handling, database schemas, APIs, React components, WebSockets, blockchain calls, and security-sensitive code.

faq.question: Does it execute commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation and workflow guidance for review. It does not include scripts or shell commands.

faq.question: Can it replace framework-specific review?
faq.answer: No. It routes work to relevant sub-skills and checklists. Detailed review still depends on the focused guidance.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it during code review, before commits, when debugging incidents, or when reviewing unfamiliar code patterns.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect grouped findings, affected categories, and checklist items that point reviewers toward likely fixes.
